map.Capstone Remix · Part 2 — part of the Bo: Capstone Remix · Part 2 — part of the Boundless arc. area, volume, expressions & distance remix · Units 5–7 + finale. Read from start to end. Each gate gives hints and a worked example. It never blocks the page.
map.Episode 2. Same crew, same city — one fo: Episode 2. Same crew, same city. One part of the case. Turn the page when you are ready.
map.Blueprint for Brightside — my favorite b: Blueprint for Brightside. My favorite build of the whole year. Today we raise a banner and bury a time capsule.
map.Capsule loot: Maya's first notebook page: Capsule loot: Maya's first notebook page, Theo's best graph, my high-score card, your tiny wrench.
map.Area covers a flat shape; volume fills a: Area covers a flat shape, and volume fills a solid. The remix: a triangle banner with base 8 and height 5, and a 3 × 2 × 4 capsule box.
map.A triangle is half the rectangle drawn a: A triangle is half of the rectangle drawn around it. A box's volume counts its unit cubes.
map.Measure twice, celebrate once. Banner an: Measure twice, celebrate once. Banner and box, reader!
map.Zara's celebration banner is a triangle:: Zara's celebration banner is a triangle: base 8 ft, height 5 ft. Find its area. The time-capsule box measures 3 × 2 × 4 ft. Find its volume.
map.Conceptual: a triangle covers exactly ha: Conceptual: a triangle covers exactly half of the rectangle drawn around it. Volume counts the unit cubes that fill a box: length × width × height.
map.Procedural: multiply base × height, then: Procedural: multiply base × height. Then take half of that. For the box, multiply the three edge lengths together in any order.
map.Below Zero taught us this grid when the: Below Zero taught us this grid when the whole city went dark. Tonight every quadrant glows.
map.And The Expression Engine left wake-up c: And The Expression Engine left wake-up code on the wall. Classic Ada. One last cipher.
map.To evaluate an expression, swap the vari: To evaluate an expression, swap the variable for its value. And when two points share a y-coordinate, their distance is just the gap along x.
map.Run the code, reader. Then draw the last: Run the code, reader. Then draw the last pattern line across the grid.
map.The wake-up code: evaluate 2n + 7 when n: The wake-up code: evaluate 2n + 7 when n = 6. Then draw the last pattern line: how many units from (−2, 3) to (4, 3)?
map.Conceptual: evaluating means swapping th: Conceptual: evaluating means swapping the letter for its number, then following the order of operations. Points that share a y-coordinate sit on one horizontal line. The distance is just the gap along x.
map.Procedural: compute 2 × n first, THEN ad: Procedural: do 2 × n first, THEN add 7. For the grid, count the steps from −2 up to 0, then from 0 over to 4. Add the two gaps.
map.Vexhall Observatory, midnight. The way h: Vexhall Observatory, midnight. The way home ran past The Balance Vault under city hall. Its brass scales, for once, were perfectly still.
map.Little fragment. Every district hums in: Little fragment. Every district hums in step because of your crew. Merge with me. Be every pattern at once. Be boundless, forever.
map.I… would know every answer. But I would: I… would know every answer. But I would stop getting to wonder.
map.VEX. It's your choice. It was always goi: VEX. It's your choice. It was always going to be your choice. We'll love you either way.
map.The Engine Heart has three locks — a pat: The Engine Heart has three locks: a pattern, a balance, and a boundary. Behind them is one question only the reader can answer.
map.The Engine Heart. Three locks — then one: The Engine Heart. Three locks, then one question with no wrong answer. Only YOUR answer.
map.Three locks guard the Engine Heart. Lock: Three locks guard the Engine Heart. Lock 1: continue Ada's pattern 5, 10, 20, 40, … Lock 2: balance her oldest equation, x + 9 = 16. Lock 3: the square engine plate has side 7. Find its perimeter. Open all three, and the Heart asks one last question. It has no wrong answer.
map.\"What is math to you?\" Every answer is: "What is math to you?" Every answer is right. Tap yours.
map.Conceptual: Lock 1 — find the rule that: Conceptual: Lock 1: find the rule that turns each term into the next. Test it on EVERY pair first. Lock 2: an equation is a balance. Ask what number keeps both sides exactly equal. Lock 3: perimeter goes around the whole boundary, and a square's four sides match.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — compute 10 ÷ 5 and: Procedural: Lock 1: compute 10 ÷ 5 and 20 ÷ 10. The factor repeats, so use it on 40. Lock 2: undo the +9 by subtracting 9 from both sides. Lock 3: multiply the side length by 4.
map.Engine — thank you. But patterns are bou: Engine, thank you. But patterns are boundless, and so are we. I choose the crew. I choose to stay small, and curious, and home.
map.Then the city keeps you both, little one: Then the city keeps you both, little one. My door stays open. Doors are patterns too.
map.Best year ever. New game plus, anyone?: Best year ever. New game plus, anyone?
map.Reader — thank you. Fifth crew member, f: Reader, thank you. Fifth crew member, first-rate. Read any volume again, any time. The gates you opened stay open, and the city remembers you.
map.Sunrise over Axiom City. AXIOM CITY WILL: Sunrise over Axiom City. AXIOM CITY WILL RETURN. Until then, the whole shelf is yours.
map.The full story — Boundless — is glowing: The full story, Boundless, glows at the city gate. — A.V.
